title: Can we guess these four cube roots without factorising?
description: The cube roots of one thousand three hundred thirty one, four thousand nine hundred thirteen, twelve thousand one hundred sixty seven and thirty two thousand seven hundred sixty eight are guessed from the last digit and the size. Each guess is then cubed to check it.
teaching_notes: One idea: the last digit of a cube gives the last digit of its root, and the size gives the tens digit. Watch for students who guess a root and never cube it to check.

video_script.why: The child finds cube roots without factorising, by fixing the last digit from the cube and the tens digit from the size, and checks each guess by cubing it.
video_script.substitution: Read the last digit of the cube to get the last digit of the root, bracket the cube between two round cubes to get the tens digit, then cube the guess to check.
video_script.anchor: four number cards, one thousand three hundred thirty one, four thousand nine hundred thirteen, twelve thousand one hundred sixty seven and thirty two thousand seven hundred sixty eight
video_script.payoff_line: The cube roots are eleven, seventeen, twenty three and thirty two

final_answer.spoken: eleven, seventeen, twenty three and thirty two

maths_rules: last digit of a cube: 1 gives 1, 2 gives 8, 3 gives 7, 4 gives 4, 5 gives 5, 6 gives 6, 7 gives 3, 8 gives 2, 9 gives 9
1331 ends in 1 and lies between 1000 and 8000, so 11; 11 × 11 = 121 and 121 × 11 = 1331
4913 ends in 3 so the root ends in 7, and lies between 1000 and 8000, so 17; 17 × 17 = 289 and 289 × 17 = 4913
12167 ends in 7 so the root ends in 3, and lies between 8000 and 27000, so 23; 23 × 23 = 529 and 529 × 23 = 12167
32768 ends in 8 so the root ends in 2, and lies between 27000 and 64000, so 32; 32 × 32 = 1024 and 1024 × 32 = 32768
video_script.design: One idea: last digit and size together fix the cube root. The four cards stay in the anchor band and each guess is built on the working board.
open_questions: The book says we are told 1331 is a perfect cube and asked to guess its cube root without factorisation, then do the same for the other three. The worklist question text drops the words without factorisation. This video follows the book, and uses the last digit and size steps given in the worklist.

narration: <bookmark mark='table'/>The last digit of a cube comes only from the last digit of its root.

<bookmark mark='round'/>The size helps too. Ten cubed is one thousand, and twenty cubed is eight thousand.
<bookmark mark='forty'/>Thirty cubed is twenty seven thousand, and forty cubed is sixty four thousand.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, four perfect cubes.

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step five, put the answers back in the question.
<bookmark mark='eleven'/>Eleven times eleven is one hundred twenty one. That times eleven is one thousand three hundred thirty one.
<bookmark mark='seventeen'/>Seventeen times seventeen is two hundred eighty nine. That times seventeen is four thousand nine hundred thirteen.
<bookmark mark='twentythree'/>Twenty three times twenty three is five hundred twenty nine. That times twenty three is twelve thousand one hundred sixty seven.
<bookmark mark='thirtytwo'/>Thirty two times thirty two is one thousand twenty four. That times thirty two is thirty two thousand seven hundred sixty eight.
